info.title: Mechbase API
info.description: API for pushing measurements and managing industrial assets.

post.summary: Trade a Microsoft sign-in code (PKCE) for a bearer token
Mint a one-time link that signs a browser in and opens `next`
post.description: For the apps' in-app browser: open `url` within 60 s and the browser is signed in as the token's user, then lands on `next`. The link works once, and dies with this token. `next` is a path on this site ("/2012/assets/5/"), an absolute URL on this host, or an `https://` URL of an http device tunnel the user may open; anything else is 422. Only a user's own unscoped bearer token may call this: a browser session, a service or MaintNode device token, an installation-scoped token or an inactive user gets 403. Limited to 10 links a minute per user (429 with Retry-After).

patch.summary: Update your name and display units
patch.description:
The web profile's name and units sheets, validated by the same form.
Only the sent fields are validated and saved; a sent null is a 422.

put.description: Idempotent upsert by external_id: 201 when created, 200 when updated. Requires external_id + name.

delete.description: Refuses with 409 when the section has zones or assets, unless ?cascade=true is passed.

post.description: Requires a parent section (section_id or section_external_id).

put.description: Idempotent PUT on the collection, keyed on external_id; requires a parent section and a name.

post.summary: Switch guest view on or off for many zones
post.description: One request, one UPDATE. Name exactly one target: `zone_ids`, every zone of `section_id`, or `all: true` for every zone of the installation. No target, more than one, or an unknown field is a 422; a zone id outside this installation is a 422 and nothing changes.

patch.description: Re-parenting a zone to another section is not allowed; delete and recreate instead.

delete.description: Refuses with 409 when the zone has assets, unless ?cascade=true is passed.

post.description: Requires a parent section (section_id or section_external_id). Zone optional, within that section.

put.description: Idempotent upsert by external_id; needs a parent section + name. Section immutable across upserts.

patch.description: Section is immutable. Zone can change within the section, or be cleared with zone_id=null.

delete.description: Refuses with 409 when the asset has measurement points, unless ?cascade=true is passed.

post.description: Requires a parent asset (asset_id or asset_external_id). PR points are auto-managed.

put.summary: Create-or-update a measurement point by external_id (upsert)
put.description: Idempotent upsert by external_id; needs a parent asset (immutable). Name auto-composed if omitted.

patch.description: The parent asset is immutable; delete and recreate to move a point.

delete.description: Refuses with 409 when the point has recorded measurements, unless ?cascade=true is passed.

get.summary: Point context: run state, staleness, limits, last 7 days
Legacy v1 URL → v2 MP map (for offline QR-code resolution)
get.description:
Return the full legacy-URL → v2 MP mapping for one installation.

Mobile clients fetch this once, cache it locally, and use it to resolve
old QR codes (encoded with v1 ``/plantlayer/<uuid>/`` or
``/measurementpoint/<uuid>/`` URLs) to the matching v2 measurement-point
detail page even when offline.

post.summary: Add a photo to an asset
post.description: Appends to the asset's photo gallery. Pass a client-minted `uuid` to make retries safe.

post.summary: Add a photo to a measurement point
post.description: Appends to the point's photos. With `keep_reference` true the reference photo does not change (a point's first photo is its reference until another is chosen). Without it, or false, the new photo also becomes the reference: what apps that predate several photos per point expect, since they replaced the photo and read `image_urls` as it. Pass a client-minted `uuid` to make retries safe.

put.summary: Choose a measurement point's reference photo
put.description: Idempotent. 404 when no photo with that uuid is attached to the point.

delete.description: 404 when no photo with that uuid is attached to the asset (already deleted counts).
404 when no photo with that uuid is attached to the point (already deleted counts).

get.description: The asset thread's comments, newest first, findings' notes included (`is_finding`). `body` is the sanitized rich-text HTML, `body_text` the same as plain text. `editable` says whether the caller wrote it, and so may change or delete it.

post.description: Adds a comment to the asset thread as the caller. `references` pins it to points of this asset, and optionally to one reading of each by `point_sequence`. A point or reading outside this asset is a 422.

patch.description: Replaces the comment's body and its whole reference set (send every reference to keep; none clears them), and marks it edited. Only the author may edit: anyone else gets a 403.

delete.description: Removes the comment and its references. Only the author may delete, and a finding's note never can be deleted (a CMMS may hold a work order against it): both are a 403.

get.description: The documents the asset page lists, newest first. Photos are not included: they are in the asset's `photos`.

post.summary: Add a document to an asset
post.description: Multipart upload of one `file` with its `kind`: drawing, datasheet, manual, check_sheet, test_report or attachment (the default). An image as a plain attachment is a photo, so it is refused here: send it to the photos endpoint, or give it a document kind. Pass a client-minted `uuid` to make retries safe.

delete.description: Anyone in the installation may delete, as on the web. 404 when no document with that uuid is attached to the asset (already deleted counts).

put.summary: Create-or-update an asset type by code (upsert)
put.description: Idempotent upsert keyed on `code`; fields left out are untouched. The checklist is validated.

patch.description: The code is the address and cannot change here.

delete.description: Assets of the type are kept, untyped.

post.summary: Add a document to an asset type
post.description: Same upload rules as an asset's documents (kind, image refusal, client-minted `uuid` for retries).
Builds the asset's checks route from its type's checklist on the first call; later calls return the same route (`created` false). 422 when the asset has no type or its type has no checklist.
Re-reads the type's checklist into the asset's checks route (`created` false). 422 once a run was completed, while one is open, or when the asset has no checks route or checklist.

Record a measurement for a point (referenced by measurement_point_id or measurement_point_external_id). Optional fields: notes/session_id/timestamp. Pass external_id to make the write idempotent: a retried push with the same external_id returns the existing reading (200) instead of creating a duplicate (201). A 409 means the external_id is already bound to a different point.

post.summary: Create many measurements in one request (partial success)
post.description: Write up to 1000 readings in a single request. Each item is processed independently and idempotently (by external_id): the results array reports created / duplicate / error per item with its index, so one bad row never sinks the batch and re-sending the whole batch is safe. For nightly-sync volumes use a service token, which is exempt from the burst/sustained limits API-wide; human tokens are throttled normally.

post.summary: Create a measurement with file attachment
post.description: Record a new measurement with a file attachment. Send as multipart/form-data with a 'payload' JSON string field and a 'file' field. Honors external_id for idempotency, same as the JSON endpoint.

get.description: Offset paginated by default (limit/offset, includes total). Pass ?cursor= for keyset pagination over long timeframes — it skips the expensive COUNT and returns next_cursor instead of total. Filter either mode by created_from / created_to (ISO-8601 with an offset or Z; a value without one is a 422).
Addressed by point_sequence, the number in the web URL (…/measurementpoints/2/measurements/766/).

patch.description: Replaces the notes (rich-text HTML, sanitized as the web editor's are). A device token gets 403.

delete.description: Deletes the reading and its files; the point's state rolls back to its newest surviving reading.

post.summary: Upload a file to an existing measurement
post.description: Attach a file to an existing measurement. File kind is auto-detected from the filename and measurement point type. Pass a client-minted `uuid` to make retries safe.

patch.description: Replace the full set of analyst-confirmed thermal hotspots on a measurement's thermogram (the iOS lightbox edit flow). Full replacement: an empty list clears all hotspots. Recomputes status = max(threshold, worst severity) and re-propagates to point/asset. No server-side detection runs.

get.summary: List the alarm rules that apply to a point
get.description: The point's own active rules (`scope` "point": overrides, its ISO 10816 default, envelope and bearing-band rules), then the installation defaults for its transducer type (`scope` "installation"). A point threshold rule takes over from the installation default's.

post.summary: Give a point its own threshold rule
post.description: Creates a point override in place of the default the point inherits (its ISO 10816 class default goes; deleting the override brings it back). Threshold rules only, absolute limits; the major limit must sit beyond the minor one. 409 when the point already has a threshold rule of its own: PATCH it. The point's status is re-evaluated at its next reading.

patch.description: Changes only the fields sent, validated as the web editor validates them. Editing the point's ISO 10816 default makes it the point's own override. Non-threshold rules are read-only (422), and so are installation defaults (403). The point's status is re-evaluated at its next reading.

delete.description: The point goes back to the default it inherits: its ISO 10816 class default (regenerated) or the installation default. Non-threshold rules are read-only (422), and so are installation defaults (403).

post.description: A route needs at least one check; `items` are in reading order and validated as the web's check form. Pass a client-minted `uuid` (and item `uuid`s) to make retries safe: a retry returns the route (200).

delete.description: Deletes the route with its runs, as the web's delete does. 409 while a run is in progress (a device may still be walking it) and for an asset's checklist route.

get.description: Newest first; cancelled runs that recorded nothing are left out (as on the web).

post.summary: Submit an item response with photo attachments
Create a route item + response during execution (field-authored)
Assign a zone-only field item to an asset

get.description: What the web run report shows: answered checks by stop with their photos and linked readings, the unanswered checks, non-conformities worst first, and totals. Works for a run in progress too.

patch.description: The finding/recommendation text on any response, as the web report's notes editor does.

post.description: Only an unanswered check of a completed run. Send `X-Idempotency-Key`: a retry returns the answer it made.

patch.description: The previous text is kept in the run's amendment log.

post.summary: Amend: add a photo to a check
post.description: On the check's response, or on its reading for a measurement check. Pass a client-minted `uuid` to make retries safe.

delete.summary: Amend: take a photo off a check
delete.description: The photo is kept on the run (not deleted). Repeating the call is a no-op.

post.summary: Amend: record a reading for a measurement check
post.description: Multipart, the web measurement form's fields: `value` (the point type's main scalar), `comment`, `images`, `data_file` (thermography: required; vibration: a value or a waveform file). A previous reading stays in the point's history. Send `X-Idempotency-Key`: a retry returns the answer it made; a key used by another reading is a 409.

get.description: Responses that were not Normal, newest run first. `status`: open (default), resolved or all.

post.description: A retry by the person who resolved it returns 200; resolved by someone else is a 409.
A new empty route and its first run in one step; checks are then added during the walk (`POST .../executions/{uuid}/items`). Pass a client-minted `uuid` for the run to make retries safe.

post.summary: Add a check to a route
post.description: Appended at the end of the route. A measurement check needs `measurement_point_id` and takes the point's asset when `asset_id` is null; a multi_check needs at least one of `subchecks`. Pass a client-minted `uuid` to make retries safe: a retry returns the check (200). 409 on an asset's checklist route.

As the web board's drag and drop: each entry's `position` orders it within its stop; `zone_id` / `asset_id` move it (null clears, omitted keeps). The route is then renumbered stop by stop, asset by asset. Returns every check's new `check_id`.

patch.description: Fields left out are kept. `subchecks` replaces a multi-check's steps (required when changing to multi_check). A type change clears the old type's config; a check cannot change to or from measurement. Move checks with reorder.

delete.description: A check that past runs answered is archived instead, so their reports keep it.

post.description: One photo per check: the new one replaces it. Pass a client-minted `uuid` to make retries safe.

get.description: Newest first, as the web check page's history.

post.description: Device reports it is online and optionally sends per-service health.
Bulk upload measurements identified by DeviceMapping UUID. The server resolves each mapping_uuid to the correct MeasurementPoint.

post.summary: Attach a file to a MaintNode measurement
post.description: Upload a binary file (e.g. .dr waveform) and attach it to an existing measurement. File kind is auto-detected from filename and measurement point type.

get.description: Each device's state, health, groups with their mapped channels, and the remote-access tunnels the caller may open (staff: all; members: http tunnels not marked staff-only). Devices needing attention come first. An http tunnel opens in a browser at `web_url`; an stcp one needs frpc and the config at `visitor_url` (staff only). `health_url` is the factory health URL, shown to staff only.

post.summary: Claim a MaintNode into the installation
post.description: The provision page's Register: claims the device, names it (`name`, optional), issues its token and queues the MECHBASE_AUTH push to Balena once the claim commits (follow `token_push`, then `is_online` for the first heartbeat). 201 when claimed; 200 when it was already in this installation, in which case its credentials are sent again and the name is not changed. 409 when another installation has it. Any member of the installation may claim; service tokens get 403.

get.summary: Look up a scanned MaintNode label
get.description: What the provision page (`/provision/<balena_uuid>/`, the label's QR) shows the caller: `claim` (free, in the fleet: claim it with POST devices), `member` (already in this installation), `taken` (in another installation, even one of the caller's), `not_found` (not in the fleet) or `unreachable` (Balena did not answer; try again). Any member of the installation may look up; service tokens get 403.

post.description: The provision page's Send credentials again: queues the push of the device's current token (issuing one only if it has none). Follow `token_push` on the returned device.

get.summary: List a MaintNode's channel slots, used and free
get.description: Per group, every channel slot its hardware has (0-15 for built-in inputs and USB DAQ, the source form's channel choices) with the point it feeds, or free. A Modbus group lists only its used register addresses (`slots` null). An inactive source still holds its slot.

post.summary: Create a group on a MaintNode
post.description: The add-source page's new group, on its own: `group_name`, `hardware_type` (hat|ul|modbus), for a USB DAQ `hardware_address` (and `hardware_id`), `interval` (s, default 1200), `sample_rate`, `samples`, and for Modbus the connection (`connection_type`, `unit_id`, `modbus_ip`, `modbus_port`, `serial_port`, `baudrate`, `parity`, `stopbits`, `bytesize`, `serial_timeout`). Same rules as that page. Returns the device; the new group is the one named `group_name`.

patch.description: The group edit page's fields: `name`, `interval` (s), `sample_rate` (Hz), `samples`; for a USB DAQ group `hardware_id` and `hardware_address`; for a Modbus group its connection (`connection_type`, `unit_id`, `modbus_ip`, `modbus_port`, `serial_port`, `baudrate`, `parity`, `stopbits`, `bytesize`, `serial_timeout`). The hardware type stays. Returns the device.

get.description: Every device's tunnels across installations, as the staff remote-access page lists them.

get.summary: Get an stcp tunnel's frpc visitor config (staff)
get.description: The connection file: run `frpc -c <file>`, then reach the service at 127.0.0.1:<local_port>. It holds the frps token and the tunnel secret.

post.summary: Add a data source to a point
post.description: Fields are the add-source page's: `source_type` (`mqtt` or `maintnode`). MQTT: `mqtt_device_id`, `mqtt_channel`. MaintNode: `device` (node uuid), then `group` (uuid) or a new group (`group_name`, `hardware_type` hat|ul|modbus, `hardware_id`, `hardware_address`, `interval`, `sample_rate`, `samples`, and the Modbus connection fields); `mn_channel` (0-15), or `register_address` for Modbus; `sensor` and its settings (`sensitivity`, `sensor_offset`, `sensor_min`, `sensor_max`, `feature`, `register_type`, `data_type`, `word_order`, `raw_scale`, `raw_offset`, `contactmode`). A MaintNode source with no `group` creates the group.

patch.description: Fields are the add-source page's: `source_type` (`mqtt` or `maintnode`). MQTT: `mqtt_device_id`, `mqtt_channel`. MaintNode: `device` (node uuid), then `group` (uuid) or a new group (`group_name`, `hardware_type` hat|ul|modbus, `hardware_id`, `hardware_address`, `interval`, `sample_rate`, `samples`, and the Modbus connection fields); `mn_channel` (0-15), or `register_address` for Modbus; `sensor` and its settings (`sensitivity`, `sensor_offset`, `sensor_min`, `sensor_max`, `feature`, `register_type`, `data_type`, `word_order`, `raw_scale`, `raw_offset`, `contactmode`). A source keeps its type, device and group; to move it, delete it and add another.

post.summary: Register this device for push notifications
post.description: Upsert by `token`: 201 when new, 200 when known (its platform, app version and last-seen time are refreshed, and a token another user registered moves to the caller). Pushes follow the caller's email notifications: same events, same notification settings.

delete.summary: Stop push notifications to this device
delete.description: 404 when the caller has no device with that token (already removed counts).

get.description: The zone page's documents: its own by kind and name, then its type's (`inherited`).

post.summary: Add a document to a zone
post.description: Multipart upload of one `file` with its `kind`: drawing, datasheet, manual, check_sheet, test_report or attachment (the default). Pass a client-minted `uuid` to make retries safe.

delete.description: The zone's own documents only (an inherited one belongs to its type). 404 when already gone.

get.description: By capture day and time, oldest first, as the zone page groups them; unknown capture times last.

post.summary: Add a concealed-works photo to a zone
post.description: Multipart upload of one image `file`; its capture time comes from the file name or EXIF. Pass a client-minted `uuid` to make retries safe. The same file (name and size) added before is not added again: 200 with the photo already there.

delete.description: 404 when no photo with that uuid is on the zone (already deleted counts).

get.description: Installation-wide flat measurement rows for BI / warehouse sync. Keyset-paginated: walk pages via next_cursor until it is null (no COUNT). Default browse mode is newest-first by measurement time. Pass ?updated_since=<ISO-8601> to switch to incremental mode: rows are returned oldest-changed-first by the updated_at watermark, so a backdated or re-finalized reading is re-emitted. The feed is at-least-once — dedupe on measurement_uuid (upsert by uuid) in the warehouse. Hard-deletes do not propagate (documented limitation). Filter by asset_id/asset_external_id, point_id/point_external_id, transducer_type, status (good|elevated|minor|major), and a created_from/created_to measurement-time window. The created_* window also constrains incremental pulls: a backdated or late-edited row whose updated_at advanced but whose measurement time falls outside the window will not re-emit, so leave created_* unset for a complete changed-since sync. ?format=csv streams the current page as CSV for a quick pull; use the export job for bulk.

get.summary: Flat alarm/audit events feed (cursor + filters + incremental)
get.description: Installation-wide audit/alarm events for BI / warehouse sync. Browse is newest-first; ?updated_since=<ISO-8601> switches to incremental, walking the immutable created_at watermark ascending. The watermark is inclusive and created_at is not unique, so the event(s) on the boundary re-emit on the next sync — at-least-once, dedupe on event_id (upsert by event_id) in the warehouse, same as the other feeds. Filter by action and a created_from/created_to window. ?format=csv streams the current page.

Installation-wide route inspection responses for BI / warehouse sync. Browse is newest-first; ?updated_since=<ISO-8601> switches to incremental by the updated_at watermark (at-least-once — dedupe on response_uuid). Filter by route_id (route uuid), status (good|elevated|minor|major), and a created_from/created_to window. ?format=csv streams the current page.

Returns the FFT arrays (freq + velocity/acceleration/envelope) for a measurement — the by-URL companion to the feed's spectra_url (arrays stay out of the row, #150). Served from the spectrum cache, else recomputed from the stored .dr waveform. Installation-scoped: the measurement must belong to the path installation (no IDOR). Empty arrays when the measurement has no waveform.

post.description: Enqueue an async CSV or Parquet export of a dataset (measurements, events, or inspections) with the same filters as the live feed. Returns 202 with a status_url to poll; when the job is done the status response carries a short-lived signed download_url. Service tokens get the full row ceiling; interactive tokens are capped lower. Bounded per-installation concurrency — 429 if too many are already in flight.

get.description: Returns the job state (pending|running|done|failed|expired). When done and not yet expired, includes a freshly-signed download_url (the signature is short-lived; re-poll to refresh it).

Streams the generated file when the signed URL is valid and unexpired and the job is still available. 403 for a bad/expired signature, 410 when the export is still building, failed, or past its file TTL.

Findings recorded by analysts, with their evidence and work-order state. Browse is newest-first. Pass ?since=<ISO-8601> for a CMMS sync: rows whose updated_at is at or after it, oldest change first, so a status change re-emits the row. The watermark is inclusive: dedupe on uuid. Filter by status (open|acknowledged|closed) and by asset or point, either by id or by external_id. Walk pages via next_cursor.

post.summary: Record a finding on a reading
post.description: The web's Record finding dialog: validated by its form (fault_type and severity from findings/choices/), the evidence derived on the server from the cursor fields. The finding is also a note on the asset's thread. 404 for an unknown point; 422 for an unknown reading or a bad field.

get.summary: Fault types and severities, and the fault a spectrum cursor suggests
get.description: The Record finding dialog's choices. With point_id and point_sequence (and the cursor: hz, amplitude, unit, signal, shaft_hz, df) it also returns the evidence the server would store and the fault type the cursor's bearing-marker match suggests (null when none).

post.description: acknowledged: a work order was raised; work_order_ref is required. closed: the work is done; work_order_ref is optional. A finding moves open -> acknowledged -> closed (open -> closed is allowed) and never back. Re-sending the current status with the same ref is a no-op, so a retried sync is safe; acknowledging again with a new ref replaces it.

get.summary: The installation's bearings, and library search
get.description: `own`: the installation's custom bearings with their point counts. `results`: with `q`, a search of the installation's and the shared library's bearings by designation and manufacturer (at most 100; a query under 2 characters finds nothing); with `order` (0 < order < 100) instead, the bearings whose defect orders match a detected tone (at most 8; `sideband` "1x" or "ftf").

post.description: All four defect orders, or none and rolling elements + ball and pitch diameter to derive them.

get.summary: One bearing (library or the installation's own)

patch.description: Only the installation's own bearings (library ones 404). Changing geometry without sending orders derives the orders from the new geometry. The fitted points' bands refresh.

delete.description: Its points lose the bearing (and its markers and band trends). Library bearings 404.

get.description:
Saved boards by position. ``is_default`` marks the board ``.../dashboards/default``
shows; with no saved board the list is the automatic board alone (``uuid`` null).

post.description: Blank name → "New dashboard". The installation's first board becomes its default.

get.description:
The web's ``dashboards/`` page: the default board, else the first, else the automatic
one. Sends an ETag; poll with ``If-None-Match`` for a 304 while nothing changed.
One saved board, sections → tiles. ETag / ``If-None-Match`` as ``.../default``.

patch.description:
The web edit form: ``name`` (required, ≤120) and ``is_default`` (true clears the
flag on every other board). Omitted or null fields keep their value.

delete.description: Deleting the default hands the flag to the next board by position.

post.description:
Persist the automatic board as "All monitored points", one section per asset.
422 when no point has an active MaintNode mapping (nothing to save).

The web's drag and drop: sections in order, each with its tiles in order (a tile may
move to another section). Sections or tiles left out keep their place; a point twice in
one section, or an id from another board, is a 422 and nothing changes.
Appended last. Blank title → "New section".

patch.description: Title required (422 when blank), cut to 120 characters.

delete.description: Deletes its tiles too.

post.description:
The add-points dialog: points appended to ``section`` in the order given; points
already in it are skipped, so the response lists only the new tiles. 404 for a section
of another board, 422 for a point id not in this installation.

patch.description: Blank label falls back to the point's own (asset · location); cut to 120 characters.

get.description: Lists the OData entity sets (Measurements, Events, Inspections) a BI connector can pull.
Static EDM document (XML) describing the entity types, generated from the feed row schemas.

get.summary: OData v4 entity set (Measurements | Events | Inspections)
get.description: Paged OData entity set over the same selectors + keyset cursor as the feeds. Supports $filter (eq/ge/le/gt/lt joined by 'and' over a per-set field whitelist), $select, $orderby (timestamp/synced_at axes), $top (total row cap), $count=true (→ @odata.count), and $skiptoken (≡ our cursor). Results are served in server-driven pages; follow @odata.nextLink until it is absent to extract the full set. Unsupported syntax → 501.

get.summary: A reading's waveform, spectra, markers and thermograms, chart-ready
get.description: What the web's reading page draws. Arrays are in `units` (the viewer's preferences); frequencies are Hz. Waveforms keep at most 4096 points (min/max per bucket), spectra at most 3200 lines (bucket max). `highpass_hz` / `lowpass_hz` reprocess the waveform as the web's Apply does (spectra cropped to the passband); each must lie in (0, fs/2) and high below low, else 422, and a reading without a waveform cannot be filtered (422). `vibration` is null without a waveform; `thermography` is null unless the point is IR or the reading has thermograms.

post.summary: The compare panel's processing: band-pass, dB, peaks
post.description: Runs the web's processing (prepare_chart_data) over up to 8 readings of this point (`cursors`, by point_sequence; empty = this reading). `type` picks the waveform (x in ms, Butterworth band-pass) or a spectrum (x in Hz, bins outside the band zeroed). Peaks are found on the full arrays, then x/y are thinned to 3200 lines / 4096 points. Values are in `units`. A cursor that is missing (or belongs to another point) or has no waveform comes back with empty arrays, in request order. A band edge outside (0, fs/2), or high-pass not below low-pass, is 422.

get.summary: Overlay spectra of up to 8 readings of one point
get.description: The point hub's compare panel. `seq` is a comma-separated list of point_sequences (at most 8, else 422); unknown ones are skipped. `spectrum` picks the signal. Each cursor's spectrum is thinned to 3200 lines in `units`; markers sit at that reading's own shaft speed; `baseline` is the envelope threshold of the first reading's operating mode. Sends an ETag (waveform files, point settings, baselines, bearing, the readings, units); a matching If-None-Match answers 304.

get.summary: The asset datasheet's trend: every point over the last 7 days
get.description: What the asset page's chart draws (asset_chart_data), values in the viewer's units: one series per non-Production point, the Production on/off samples for the background bands, and the window it spans (7 days back from the asset's latest reading). `type` narrows the series to one transducer type. At most 40,000 readings per request. Timestamps carry the server's local offset.

get.summary: Pre/post fault record: the asset's points over at ± 60 s
get.description: Every scalar point with readings within 60 s of `at` (ISO-8601; without an offset it is read in the server's time zone), in native units, with each point's alarm limits. `point` names the point whose reading raised the change, echoed as trigger_point_id when it is on this asset.

post.summary: Relearn a point's normal range from a date
post.description: Queues the background fit over the readings on and after `refit_from` (not in the future). 422 when fewer than 100 usable readings exist since then (see the preview).

delete.summary: Clear a point's learned normal range
delete.description: Removes its operating modes and spectral baselines; it falls back to the standard ISO limits.

get.summary: How many readings a relearn from a date would use
get.description: `since` (YYYY-MM-DD, optional): count usable readings on or after it; `fit_min` is the minimum.

get.summary: The installation home: status, needs attention, routes, back to normal, sections
Every asset needing attention (or, with show=silent, every silent asset)
get.description:
The web's alerts page: non-Normal assets worst first, then silent ones.
``show=silent`` lists every silent asset instead, whatever its status.

get.summary: Recent activity: status changes, notes, findings and route completions, newest first
Search the installation: counts per category and typed results
get.description:
The web's search page. ``q`` under 2 characters finds nothing. ``in``
(a category ``slug``) fills only that list, with more rows (50); without
it every list holds its first few (assets 15, the rest 10).

get.summary: Running hours of every production-tracked asset
get.description:
The web's Running hours page over a window of local days (``tz``):
``production_from`` / ``production_to`` are ISO dates, a malformed one is
ignored. Neither: today. From alone: that day's start to now. To alone:
the day before that day's end. ``window_start`` / ``window_end`` say
what was used.

post.summary: Flip the asset's current production state (running ⇄ stopped) now

get.summary: Your email notification settings for this installation

patch.summary: Change your email notification settings for this installation
patch.description:
Unsent fields keep their value; a sent null is a 422.
``notifications_muted`` is account-wide. A service token gets 403.

post.summary: Send yourself a test notification email now
post.description:
Sent at once, muted or not. 422 when your account has no email address,
502 when the mail provider refused it. A service token gets 403.

image_urls.title: Image Urls

bearing.description: A library bearing or this installation's own; null removes it.
bearing.title: Bearing

envelope_band_low.description: Envelope band lower edge, Hz (>= 1); null = default.
envelope_band_low.title: Envelope Band Low

envelope_band_high.description: Upper edge, Hz, above the lower; null = default.
envelope_band_high.title: Envelope Band High

instructions.description: Rich-text HTML; '' (or the type default) clears it.
instructions.title: Instructions

PointContextOut.description: A point's default key in native units: run state, staleness, limits, last 7 days (6 h means).
PointContextOut.title: PointContextOut

body.description: Rich-text HTML; sanitized on save like the web composer's.
body.title: Body

point_id.description: A measurement point of this asset.
point_id.title: Point Id

point_sequence.description: One reading of that point, by its point_sequence.
point_sequence.title: Point Sequence

HotClusterIn.description:
A client-supplied (analyst-confirmed) thermal hotspot.

The iOS app runs detection on-device, an analyst confirms it, and pushes
the result. ``severity`` is a ``common.models.Status`` integer from the
same NETA bucketing the server uses; ``source`` is an audit-only hint
("auto" | "manual"). Coordinates are percentages of the frame so they
render unchanged by the existing overlay. See ``HotspotsIn`` /
``MeasurementIn.hot_clusters``.
HotClusterIn.title: HotClusterIn

TachIn.description:
Tachometer pulse positions captured with a vibration waveform.

``edges`` are sample indices into the waveform, ``fs`` its sample rate,
``ppr`` pulses per revolution and ``lag`` the tach channel's delay (s).
Stored on ``Measurement.meta_data["tach"]``, never in ``data``.
TachIn.title: TachIn

MeasurementBatchResultOut.description:
Per-item outcome for a batch write. ``status`` is one of created /
duplicate / error. ``duplicate`` means an idempotent hit (external_id was
already recorded) — the existing reading is returned unchanged.
MeasurementBatchResultOut.title: MeasurementBatchResultOut

MeasurementNotesIn.description: A reading's notes, as rich-text HTML (sanitized on save, like the web editor's).
MeasurementNotesIn.title: MeasurementNotesIn

HotspotsIn.description:
Body for the hotspot-edit PATCH endpoint. Full replacement: the list
given replaces all stored hotspots, and ``[]`` clears them.
HotspotsIn.title: HotspotsIn

source.description: How the rule came about when not set by hand: "iso_10816" (the ISO class default) and so on.
source.title: Source

AlarmRuleIn.description:
A point threshold override. Validated by the web editor's form
(``PointAlarmRuleForm``), so the API stores only what the web would.
PATCH reads only the fields sent.

method.description: Only "threshold" is writable over the API.
method.title: Method

data_key.description: The reading the limits apply to; blank for the transducer type's default.
data_key.title: Data Key

direction.description: "high": above the limit is bad; "low": below it is.
direction.title: Direction

threshold_mode.description: "absolute" limits. "relative" (multiples of a baseline) is for bearing bands only.
threshold_mode.title: Threshold Mode

AlarmRuleIn.title: AlarmRuleIn

StartConflictOut.description:
409 body for a refused execution start.

``running_execution_uuid`` is set when the refusal is because the route
already has an in-progress execution (a route runs at most once at a time):
the client should join that execution and re-point anything it queued
against its own uuid. It is null for the other 409 (a client uuid that
already belongs to a different route).
StartConflictOut.title: StartConflictOut

StartExecutionIn.description:
Optional body for starting a route execution.

Lets offline-first native clients mint the execution `uuid` locally and push
the start through their outbox when connectivity returns (item responses and
measurements already work this way). Both fields are optional, and a caller
that POSTs no body — or `{}` — keeps the original server-minted behavior so
the browser/web UI is unaffected. See issue #181.
StartExecutionIn.title: StartExecutionIn

ExecutionSummaryOut.description:
One run in a route's history. Counts are over the run's responses, as
the web's Runs table shows them: ``passed_count``/``answered_count``.
ExecutionSummaryOut.title: ExecutionSummaryOut

FieldItemIn.description:
Create a RouteItem + ItemResponse in one call (field-authored survey item).

The item is zone-anchored (or route-level with ``zone_id=None``); the
technician triages it to a specific asset later via ``/triage``.
FieldItemIn.title: FieldItemIn

ReadingOut.description: The Measurement a measurement check's response links to.
ReadingOut.title: ReadingOut

HardwareIn.description:
What the device detected. Any key may be missing (an older device, a probe that did not run); unknown keys
are dropped, so a device cannot grow the row without bound.
HardwareIn.title: HardwareIn

ModbusProbeIn.description: One Modbus connection the device tried: where, and whether it answered. Unknown keys are dropped.
ModbusProbeIn.title: ModbusProbeIn

ExportFiltersIn.description:
Union of all feed filters for a bulk export request body. All optional +
length-bounded; the POST whitelists the subset relevant to the dataset.
ExportFiltersIn.title: ExportFiltersIn

FindingOut.description:

Mechbase's ids and the caller-owned ``external_id`` the sync keys on.
FindingOut.title: FindingOut

FindingIn.description:
Record a finding on a reading, as the web's Record finding dialog does.

The cursor fields (``hz`` … ``df``) are where the analyst clicked the
spectrum; the server derives the stored evidence (marker match, order,
bearing) from them, never from what the client claims it matched.

shaft_hz.title: Shaft Hz

df.description: The spectrum's line spacing, Hz (widens the marker match).
df.title: Df

FindingIn.title: FindingIn

FindingStatusIn.description:
Move a finding on: ``acknowledged`` (a work order was raised; the ref is
required) or ``closed`` (the work is done; a ref may be added).
FindingStatusIn.title: FindingStatusIn

point_count.description: Points fitted with it; own bearings in the list only.
point_count.title: Point Count

BearingIn.description:
A custom bearing: all four defect orders, or none and the geometry
(rolling elements, ball and pitch diameter, contact angle) to derive them.
PATCH reads only the fields sent.
BearingIn.title: BearingIn
